18.title: Tree split and Gini impurity
18.before:
Imagine sorting a mixed box of toys into separate piles by type. Gini impurity is a score that measures how mixed up a group of items is.

A score of zero means the group is completely pure and contains only one kind of thing.
18.after:
When items are split into different branches, we want each branch to become less mixed than before. The impurity score helps decision trees decide the best way to divide data into clear groups.

Lower scores mean the sorting worked well and the resulting piles are clean.

76.title: Forward diffusion with known noise
76.before:
Forward diffusion corrupts a clean latent vector by mixing it with sampled Gaussian noise according to predefined noise schedules.

Each step scales the original signal down while scaling the noise up to preserve variance.
76.after: Examining individual cells shows how the clean value and noise combine linearly to form the noisy latent. The resulting tensor serves as the training target for the denoising network.

159.title: Steps down a hill to find the lowest spot
159.before:
Imagine you are blindfolded on a hilly terrain and want to walk down to the lowest valley. You feel the slope with your feet and step in the direction that goes down most steeply.

By repeating this small step again and again, you eventually reach the bottom.
159.after: Gradient descent is a computer algorithm that does the exact same thing to find the best settings for a task. The slope is called the error, and the goal is to reach zero error by tweaking parameters.

194.title: Causal mask on decoder scores
194.before:
The transformer decoder prevents models from reading future context by applying a causal mask to attention scores. When predicting the word sat, the model must not access later words like on or mat.

Look for the masked cells in the upper right triangle of the heatmap below where future positions are blocked.
194.after:
This matrix sets forbidden positions to negative infinity before the softmax function runs. Because softmax exponentiates these values, the blocked future positions receive exactly zero weight.

As a result, each query position can only attend to current and preceding tokens in the sequence.

203.title: Causal masking before softmax
203.before:
The decoder prevents attending to future tokens by adding an additive causal mask $M$ to the attention scores before the softmax operation.

For query position $i$ and key position $j$, the mask value is $M_{ij} = 0$ if $j \le i$ and $M_{ij} = -\infty$ if $j > i$.

Examine the heatmap below to see how upper-triangle entries receive negative infinity.
203.after: When exponentiated during row-wise $\operatorname{softmax}$, these $-\infty$ entries evaluate to zero weight. This ensures that token representations only depend on past and present positions.
